get.description: `code` is what follows `/join/` in the group's link, read in any case. Its name, monogram, club and district, sport dots and member count — **and never who is in it**.

404.description: `group_not_found` — a link that leads nowhere: no group has that code, it could be no group's, or its group was deleted.

post.summary: What an invitation's link opens, on the invitation page
post.description: Read before anything is set, whatever the link's state: the name to greet, the club, whether the link still works — and its code while it does. The club's reset of an administrator opens this page too. Changes nothing.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link never issued as an invitation: a password reset's link included.

post.summary: Set your password here, by the invitation's link
post.description: **The same rules and the same results as the app's *Set your password***: a new person's account is created — no player name, no nickname, no Adult attestation — or an account the club reset gets its password back, and either way the administrator is active and the link is spent. **Nobody is signed in**: the page then says to open Rakieta and sign in with this email and password.

400.description: `password_too_weak` (`details.field`: `password`) — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit. The link and the code still work.

409.description: The invitation can no longer be used: `credential_expired` (ask the club to send a new one), `credential_used`, `credential_locked` (five wrong codes) — or `sign_in_to_accept`: the email has an account now, which accepts from the app, signed in.

post.summary: Whether a reset's link still works
post.description: Read before anything is set, whatever the link's state — its state and nothing else. Changes nothing.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link never issued as a player's or an administrator's reset: a club's, or an invitation's, included.

post.summary: Set a new password by a reset's link, and sign out everywhere
post.description: **The same rules and the same results as the app's *Forgot password?***: the password rule, the link spent, and **every session signed out** — every access token issued before this moment is refused (`access_token_revoked`) and every refresh token revoked. **Nobody is signed in**: the page then says to open Rakieta and sign in with the new password.

400.description: `password_too_weak` (`details.field`: `password`) — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit. The link and the code still work.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link never issued as a player's or an administrator's reset: a club's, or an invitation's, included.

get.summary: Who a friend link is from
get.description: `code` is what follows `/f/` in the link, read in any case. The owner's nickname and first photograph — **and nothing else about them**.

404.description: `friend_link_not_found` — *Nothing at that link*: the code was replaced by a New link, no link ever carried it, or it could be no link's.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response, on both API surfaces.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this exact failure. The only half of the envelope a client may branch on.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Never the copy shown to a user — that is the client's, chosen from the code.
message.title: Message

trace_id.description: This request's identifier, also returned on the X-Request-ID header. Ties a client-side failure to a server log without logging a payload.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

details.description: Structured context for this code, when the code defines any.
details.title: Details

InvitationByTokenRequest.title: InvitationByTokenRequest
InvitationByTokenRequest.description:
The token off an invitation's link. In a body rather than a path, so it
is in no access log.

InvitationLinkState.title: InvitationLinkState
InvitationLinkState.description:
Whether an invitation's link still works — the credential's standing,
under a name of its own on the wire (``Standing`` is a challenge's).

InvitationPagePasswordRequest.title: InvitationPagePasswordRequest
InvitationPagePasswordRequest.description:
*Set your password here*, on the invitation page: the link's `token`
and the password — **never a ticket**, since the page holds the link and a
claimed code is the app's way in.

The password carries no bound here, exactly as in the app: 8 to 128
characters with a letter and a digit, refused as `password_too_weak`
naming the field.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name the club typed, **whole** — *Marta Wójcik*, never a first name cut out of it. It is the Administrator's and stays theirs: the account a password opens holds no player name (``docs/adr/0199`` §4).

state.description: `valid`, `expired` (ask the club to send a new one), `used`, or `locked` — five wrong codes.

code.title: Code
code.description: The 8-character code the email carries under its button, for *after you install, open Rakieta and enter this code* — **only while `valid`**, `null` otherwise.

InvitationPageResponse.title: InvitationPageResponse
InvitationPageResponse.description:
What the invitation page greets with — **the least it needs**
(``docs/adr/0187`` §5), and no email: the page locks no field to it.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: Their first photograph, a link that expires within minutes; `null` when they have none.

LinkedFriendResponse.title: LinkedFriendResponse
LinkedFriendResponse.description:
A Friend link's owner as the public site's `/f/<code>` page draws them for
somebody who has not signed in — *{nickname} invited you to play on
Rakieta* — **and nothing else about them**.

LinkedGroupClubSchema.title: LinkedGroupClubSchema
LinkedGroupClubSchema.description: Where the group plays, as the page's line under its name.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order, by the rule every surface draws them by. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read now. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: How many are in it — the same count the app draws.

LinkedGroupResponse.title: LinkedGroupResponse
LinkedGroupResponse.description:
A group as its link's page draws it for somebody who has not signed in —
and the preview a messenger draws from that page (``docs/adr/0187`` §4).
**The least that page needs, and nobody in the group**: no member, Owner or
administrator is named, counted apart or pictured (§5).

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The first character of each of the first two words, as typed, or the first two characters of a one-word name: *my rakieta group* is `mr`, *Ogrody 33 Club* is `O3`. Draw it as it comes — never change its case.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: A colour **key** from 0 to 7, fixed for the group for ever — derived from its id, so a rename keeps it. Map it to your own palette; the backend never names a colour.

MonogramSchema.title: MonogramSchema
MonogramSchema.description:
The group's tile, **cut by the backend** so every client draws the same
one (``docs/adr/0183`` §5).

ResetLinkState.title: ResetLinkState
ResetLinkState.description:
Whether a reset's link still works — the credential's standing, under a
name of its own on the wire.

ResetPagePasswordRequest.title: ResetPagePasswordRequest
ResetPagePasswordRequest.description:
*Set a new password* on the reset page: the link's `token` and the
password — **never a ticket**, since the page holds the link and a claimed
code is the app's way in.

The password carries no bound here, exactly as in the app: 8 to 128
characters with a letter and a digit, refused as `password_too_weak`
naming the field.

ResetPageRequest.title: ResetPageRequest
ResetPageRequest.description:
The token off a reset's link. In a body rather than a path, so it is in
no access log.

state.description: `valid`; `expired` — after an hour, or once a newer email was asked for: ask again; `used`; or `locked` — five wrong codes.

ResetPageResponse.title: ResetPageResponse
ResetPageResponse.description:
What the reset page reads off its link — **its state and nothing else**
(``docs/adr/0187`` §5): not whose it is, and not its code.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Rakieta rates, as a closed enum.
